meta.title: Six nights after forever
meta.methodology: Research captured August 2026. Rates are planning ranges and confidence labels distinguish exact-date observations from adjacent-date, generic signals, and estimates.

hotels.name: Palm Heights
hotels.summary: The most distinctive and couple-scaled choice: 52 ocean-view suites, a sharp Caribbean design point of view, serious food, and the Garden Club wellness campus without the feel of a conventional mega-resort.
hotels.bestRoom: One Bedroom Oceanfacing Terrace Suite
hotels.priceNote: Direct SynXis results checked for Oct 5–11, 2026 showed one-bedroom suites at $934–$1,074 per night before taxes and fees; the displayed all-in range normalizes 13% accommodation tax, an observed 10% service-charge signal, and a reported $90 nightly resort fee. Reconfirm the final checkout total before booking.
hotels.weather: Hot, humid wet-season conditions: roughly 89°F daytime / 78°F nighttime norms, warm sea, sun mixed with tropical showers.
hotels.weatherRisk: High. Early October is still in the wet season; September and October are the rainfall maxima, and Atlantic hurricane season runs through November 30.
hotels.route: MIA → GCM nonstop; GCM → SFO requires at least one connection, most cleanly via MIA on American when schedules align.
hotels.travelFriction: Low inbound, moderate outbound: about a 15-minute transfer from GCM, but no nonstop flight to SFO and an international connection on the return.
hotels.honestCatch: It is the strongest aesthetic fit, but not a secluded hideaway: the beach, restaurants, and social programming have a fashionable scene, and October weather can interrupt a beach-first plan.

hotels.name: Hotel Wailea
hotels.summary: A 72-suite, adults-only Relais & Châteaux retreat on 15 hillside acres: intimate, residential and far removed from Hawai‘i’s family mega-resort pattern.
hotels.bestRoom: Celebration Ocean View Suite
hotels.priceNote: No usable Oct 5–11 checkout quote was captured. This is an estimated all-in planning range; request a refundable six-night total including taxes and any mandatory charges. Andaz Maui is intentionally excluded from this set because its posted Sep 7–Nov 14, 2026 renovation overlaps the stay.
hotels.weather: Warm, trade-wind early October; south Maui is among the drier island microclimates, with hot beach days and occasional brief showers.
hotels.route: MIA → OGG requires a connection; OGG → SFO has nonstop service on selected schedules. Wailea is roughly 25–35 minutes from OGG.
hotels.honestCatch: It is not beachfront and has a smaller on-property activity campus; the value case depends on a live all-in quote below the hard ceiling.

hotels.name: Wickaninnish Inn
hotels.summary: A deeply romantic, locally owned oceanfront inn where cedar, surf, fireplaces, and Chesterman Beach make bad weather part of the point. It is the most transportive option here and the best value at this level, but reaching it from Miami and then leaving for San Francisco consumes real time and carries weather risk.
hotels.bestRoom: Third-floor Premier Room in the Pointe Building for the clearest surf and sunset sightlines
hotels.priceNote: Not a live availability quote. The inn publishes October 1–31, 2026 Premier Room rates of CAD 940–1,120 before tax, depending on floor and weekday/weekend. This USD range estimates Canadian taxes and an approximate exchange rate; breakfast is extra. October 5–11 availability still needs confirmation.
hotels.weather: October is storm-season shoulder weather: roughly 55°F/48°F, cool and windy, with rain on about 19 days and around 13 inches across the month. Bring real waterproofs and expect some days to be indoor, spa, fireplace, or storm-watching days.
hotels.weatherRisk: High — heavy rain, low cloud, wind, and small-aircraft disruption are plausible; this is only a good choice if moody weather sounds romantic rather than disappointing.
hotels.route: MIA → YVR, then either a weather-sensitive small-plane hop from YVR South to Tofino/Long Beach or a connection to Nanaimo plus roughly 3 hours of winding island driving. Outbound requires reversing to YVR before YVR → SFO; protect the SFO connection with a long buffer or Vancouver overnight.
hotels.travelFriction: Very high — border crossing, at least one extra flight or a long island drive, and weather-sensitive connections at both ends
hotels.honestCatch: Six nights could feel gloriously elemental or very wet and isolated; the route is too fragile for a tight same-day connection to SFO.

hotels.name: Kona Village, A Rosewood Resort
hotels.summary: Standalone kauhale, lava-and-ocean landscape, cultural and marine programming, and an Asaya spa built into the lava flow create the strongest sense of place in the field.
hotels.bestRoom: Beach Front One-Bedroom Kauhale
hotels.priceNote: No exact-date rate or availability was returned. This high, wide all-in estimate reflects the premium room product and Hawaiʻi taxes; obtain a written six-night total before considering it within budget.
hotels.weather: Hot and generally dry on the leeward Kona coast in early October, though Kona storms can interrupt the normal pattern as the wetter season approaches.
hotels.route: MIA → KOA requires a protected mainland connection; KOA → SFO has nonstop options. The resort is roughly 20 minutes from KOA.
hotels.honestCatch: It can exceed the $2,500 all-in ceiling, and recent evidence is mixed on service and food-and-beverage execution despite the extraordinary setting.

hotels.name: Montage Healdsburg
hotels.summary: A polished 258-acre resort threaded through oak woodland and vines, with bungalow-style rooms, serious service, two pools, a strong spa, and easy Healdsburg access. It delivers effortless luxury and activities without forcing a schedule, though it feels more like a grand resort than a private inn.
hotels.bestRoom: Deluxe Vineyard King for a balcony fire pit and direct vineyard outlook
hotels.priceNote: Generic 2026 rate signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Public current rates commonly begin around USD 850–1,100 before tax; October harvest weekends can run much higher. Range estimates 16% room tax, the reported USD 60 nightly resort fee, and likely room-category spread.
hotels.weather: Early October is usually warm, dry harvest weather: days in the mid-to-upper 70s and cool nights near 50°F, with large day/night swings.
hotels.weatherRisk: Low to medium — rain is uncommon, but heat spikes, wildfire smoke, and harvest-season crowds remain the meaningful fall risks.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then roughly 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 15 minutes by car via US-101. Return to SFO on October 11 with extra Sunday traffic buffer.
hotels.travelFriction: Moderate — one straightforward flight and drive, but Bay Area and Wine Country traffic can add an hour
hotels.honestCatch: At 130 rooms with family programming and two pools, it can read as impeccably managed resort luxury rather than a singular honeymoon hideaway.

hotels.name: Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
hotels.summary: Fresh from a roughly $240 million transformation, Mauna Kea combines a superb swimmable crescent beach, new adult infinity pool and spa, manta viewing, golf, tennis and cultural programming.
hotels.bestRoom: Renovated Beachfront Wing Oceanfront King
hotels.priceNote: AFAR reported rates from $998 including breakfast for two, with other current signals around $1,100–$1,200 including taxes and fees. This is a non-date all-in target for a worthwhile ocean room.
hotels.weather: Warm, dry Kohala Coast conditions around 86°F/74°F historically, with low rainfall and excellent early-October odds.
hotels.route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstops. The hotel is roughly 35–45 minutes from KOA.
hotels.honestCatch: It remains a multigenerational legacy resort rather than an intimate hideaway, and food-and-beverage consistency is the recurring weak spot.

hotels.name: Post Ranch Inn
hotels.summary: The emotional high-water mark: forty adults-only rooms folded into a 1,200-foot Big Sur bluff, with extraordinary privacy, architecture, ocean pools, Sierra Mar, and no televisions. It is the clearest minimoon fantasy here, but likely exceeds the hard all-in ceiling on most October dates.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean House, preferably a northern unit with outdoor soaking tub
hotels.priceNote: Generic current signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Recent public rates cluster around USD 2,000–3,000 before or around taxes depending on source and room. Breakfast and many activities are included; premium ocean rooms can run beyond this range.
hotels.weather: October is one of Big Sur’s better months: typically upper 60s by day and low 50s at night, with fog and wind possible and rainfall beginning to increase later in the month.
hotels.weatherRisk: Medium — the climate is usually favorable, but Highway 1 is vulnerable to fire, rockfall, and emergency closures even outside winter.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then about 2 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours 30 minutes south via US-101, CA-156, and Highway 1 from Monterey. As of August 11, 2026, Caltrans reported a wildfire closure from Fernwood to north of Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park; the inn sits within this Big Sur corridor, so verify Caltrans QuickMap immediately before committing and again before driving.
hotels.travelFriction: High right now — normally a scenic but long drive; the active Highway 1 wildfire closure makes present access uncertain
hotels.honestCatch: This is probably the best pure minimoon experience and the least defensible financially; six nights can exceed USD 20,000 before flights and transfers.

quote.text: High atop the cliffs of Big Sur, the striking views and otherworldly serenity can’t help but stir your soul.

hotels.name: Ko‘a Kea Resort on Poʻipū Beach
hotels.summary: A low-rise 121-room oceanfront hotel with couple-forward energy, Red Salt, yoga and beach access—Kauaʻi’s clearest conventional minimoon hotel.
hotels.bestRoom: Oceanfront King
hotels.priceNote: Michelin’s October calendar showed roughly $968 with free cancellation, but not a captured Oct 5–11 checkout. This all-in range allows for resort fee, parking and Hawaiʻi taxes; confirm the oceanfront premium.
hotels.weather: Warm and comparatively dry on Kauaʻi’s south shore, with better October reliability than Princeville.
hotels.route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstops. Poʻipū is roughly 25–35 minutes from LIH.
hotels.honestCatch: The room hardware is slightly dated—dark wood, carpet and not-very-private lanais—and the pool and spa are compact. Book only oceanfront.

hotels.name: Alila Ventana Big Sur
hotels.summary: An adults-only 160-acre redwood retreat where meals, nonalcoholic drinks, wellness programming, valet parking, and many experiences are folded into the rate. It is more active and social than Post Ranch, with better value clarity, two pools, Japanese baths, and strong rooms with fireplaces and decks.
hotels.bestRoom: Vista Hot Tub Suite for a private soaking tub, fireplace, and forest-and-coast atmosphere
hotels.priceNote: Generic current all-inclusive signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Public 2026 rates span roughly USD 1,900–3,000+ with estimated taxes and fees. Dining and many resort experiences are included, improving the effective comparison but not bringing most dates under the ideal budget.
hotels.weather: Expect mild upper-60s days, low-50s nights, coastal fog, and cool redwood shade. Early October is often dry, though the rainy season statistically begins around this week.
hotels.weatherRisk: Medium — pleasant weather is likely, but fog, first rains, wildfire activity, and Highway 1 closures can override the forecast.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then about 2 hours 45 minutes to 3 hours 30 minutes south through Monterey. The August 11, 2026 Caltrans wildfire closure spans Fernwood to north of Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park and affects the Ventana corridor; do not treat current road access as normal until Caltrans reopens it.
hotels.travelFriction: High right now — normally manageable from SFO via the north, but active emergency closure status must be resolved before booking
hotels.honestCatch: The inclusions soften the sticker shock, but the resort can still break the USD 2,500 all-in nightly cap, and shared programming makes it less hushed than Post Ranch.

hotels.name: Farmhouse Inn
hotels.summary: A 25-room hideaway in the Russian River Valley that feels personal rather than programmed, pairing whitewashed cottages and barn suites with notably warm service, serious food, a small spa, and concierge-led winery access. It is the strongest balance of intimacy, quality, route sanity, and budget.
hotels.bestRoom: Barn Junior Suite for privacy, fireplace, soaking tub, and enough space without paying for the largest suite
hotels.priceNote: Generic rate signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Current public examples range from about USD 694 all-in for an entry room to roughly USD 1,330 all-in for a Barn One-Bedroom Suite on non-October dates; harvest demand may push higher.
hotels.weather: Early October usually brings warm, dry afternoons in the 70s and crisp nights around 50°F — excellent for vineyards, terraces, and fire pits.
hotels.weatherRisk: Low to medium — the practical risks are a heat spike or regional wildfire smoke, not sustained rain.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then roughly 1 hour 40 minutes to 2 hours 15 minutes north via US-101 and River Road. The return to SFO is straightforward with traffic buffer.
hotels.travelFriction: Moderate — easiest of the intimate rural options, with no ferry, secondary flight, or cliff highway
hotels.honestCatch: It is a romantic base, not a self-contained grand resort; after several nights, the trip works best if you genuinely want winery drives and dinners out.

quote.text: A 25-room hideaway in Sonoma’s Russian River Valley, Farmhouse Inn is where the table, the land, and genuine hospitality come together with uncommon ease.

hotels.name: Kimpton Seafire Resort + Spa
hotels.location: Northern Seven Mile Beach, Grand Cayman
hotels.summary: The easiest all-rounder: contemporary ocean-view rooms, a notably strong spa and dining lineup, and a quieter northern stretch of Seven Mile Beach, with enough resort infrastructure to make a weather-disrupted day painless.
hotels.bestRoom: 1 King Premium Ocean View
hotels.priceNote: A researched all-in planning range rather than a captured Oct 5–11 checkout quote. It triangulates low-season public rate signals with the current $95 nightly resort-fee disclosure and Cayman taxes/service charges; reprice directly with IHG before relying on it.
hotels.weather: Hot, humid wet-season conditions: roughly 89°F daytime / 78°F nighttime norms, warm sea, sun mixed with tropical showers.
hotels.weatherRisk: High. Early October is still in the wet season; September and October are the rainfall maxima, and Atlantic hurricane season runs through November 30.
hotels.route: MIA → GCM nonstop; GCM → SFO requires at least one connection, with MIA, DFW, ATL, or IAH the usual practical gateways depending on airline and day.
hotels.travelFriction: Low inbound, moderate outbound: about a 15–20-minute transfer from GCM, then a one-stop-or-more return to SFO with no nonstop option.
hotels.honestCatch: It is polished and highly capable, but 264 rooms and a family-friendly program make it feel more like a full resort than an intimate honeymoon cocoon.

hotels.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Grand Cayman
hotels.summary: The maximalist service-and-amenities choice: oceanfront rooms, Blue by Eric Ripert, a renewed spa, golf, tennis, watersports, and deep bench strength when the goal is effortless rather than boutique.
hotels.bestRoom: Oceanfront Ocean Tower Balcony Room
hotels.priceNote: A researched all-in planning range rather than a captured Oct 5–11 checkout quote. It uses public October/low-season rate signals, Cayman tax/service assumptions, and the currently reported $110 nightly resort fee; verify the live Marriott total and room tower before booking.
hotels.weather: Hot, humid wet-season conditions: roughly 89°F daytime / 78°F nighttime norms, warm sea, sun mixed with tropical showers.
hotels.weatherRisk: High. Early October is still in the wet season; September and October are the rainfall maxima, and Atlantic hurricane season runs through November 30.
hotels.route: MIA → GCM nonstop; GCM → SFO requires at least one connection, with MIA, DFW, ATL, or IAH the usual practical gateways depending on airline and day.
hotels.travelFriction: Low inbound, moderate outbound: roughly a 10–15-minute transfer from GCM, then a one-stop-or-more return to SFO with no nonstop option.
hotels.honestCatch: The resort is large, family-oriented, and split across road-linked towers; choose the Ocean Tower carefully or the experience can feel more conference grand-hotel than minimoon retreat.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Resort Hualālai
hotels.summary: Extensively renovated rooms, five restaurants, King’s Pond, marine-biologist programming, manta snorkeling, golf and volcanic excursions make this the safest full-service choice.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean-View Prime King Room
hotels.priceNote: No Oct 5–11 quote was captured. Public non-date signals ran from roughly $1,330 for standard rooms to above $2,000 for ocean views before the full Hawaiʻi tax stack; this is an all-in planning range.
hotels.weather: Hot, sunny leeward-coast weather is the baseline, with low rain risk relative to Kauaʻi and windward locations.
hotels.route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstops. The resort is roughly 15 minutes from KOA.
hotels.honestCatch: It is large and family-oriented, and the ocean-view category most worth booking may land at or above the hard all-in ceiling.

hotels.name: Mauna Lani, Auberge Collection
hotels.summary: A renovated Kohala Coast resort with a real spa, broad cultural and ocean programming, golf and a calm bay—capable without Hualālai or Kona Village pricing.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean View King
hotels.priceNote: No exact October quote was captured. A separate-date signal started near $848 including taxes and fees; this all-in planning range adds room-category spread plus the official $60 resort fee and likely $40 parking.
hotels.weather: Warm, dry and sunny on the leeward Kohala Coast, with among the best early-October weather odds in Hawaiʻi.
hotels.route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstop options. Mauna Lani is about 30 minutes from KOA.
hotels.honestCatch: At 333 rooms it is a full resort, not a hideaway; the beach is a calm lagoon, and the $60 resort fee plus parking erodes the apparent value.

hotels.name: 1 Hotel Hanalei Bay
hotels.summary: The field’s most dramatic setting pairs Hanalei Bay views with serious wellness, three heated pools, ocean access and nature-led design.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean View Terrace King with a confirmed real terrace
hotels.priceNote: A third-party Oct 5–11 signal showed $9,382.63 before tax for six nights, with the $59 nightly resort fee included; the all-in range adds the listed tax stack and valet allowance. Reconfirm directly. Signature Welina Terrace is closed Oct 5–30, 2026, with a pop-up replacing it.
hotels.weather: Warm and lush, with the highest rain risk in this Hawaiʻi set as Princeville moves into the wetter season; showers can be localized but materially affect a beach-first stay.
hotels.route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstop options. Princeville is roughly 50–60 minutes from LIH.
hotels.honestCatch: Welina Terrace is closed for the entire stay, service consistency has drawn credible complaints, and many standard rooms lack a true terrace; book only a confirmed terrace room on a refundable rate.

hotels.name: The Lodge at Kukui‘ula
hotels.summary: A one-bedroom club bungalow delivers a private island home plus an adult pool, spa, farm, golf, racquets, dining and adventure programming.
hotels.bestRoom: One-Bedroom Platinum Club Bungalow with exact unit guaranteed
hotels.priceNote: Nearby-date entry inventory was around $1,182 with estimated taxes and fees. This all-in target includes a cushion for the official 15% destination fee, $150 reservation fee and damage waiver; exact Oct 5–11 inventory was not verified.
hotels.weather: Warm and comparatively dry in sunny Poʻipū; the south shore is the safer Kauaʻi weather bet in October.
hotels.route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstops. The Lodge is roughly 25–35 minutes from LIH.
hotels.honestCatch: This is a residential/private-club product rather than a conventional hotel, it has no direct swimmable beach, and the 15% destination fee materially changes the total.

hotels.summary: A quiet, high-service resort above Mānele Bay with a broad island program and genuine remove from the family-resort circuit.
hotels.bestRoom: Prime Ocean Front King Room
hotels.priceNote: A Michelin-indexed non-date signal was about $1,567 with taxes. This broader all-in range is not proof of Oct 5–11 availability; obtain a cancellable quote. Eligible room bookings include round-trip Honolulu–Lānaʻi flights through 2027.
hotels.weather: Warm and generally dry around Mānele Bay, with trade winds and a lower rain risk than Kauaʻi’s north shore.
hotels.route: MIA → HNL requires a connection, followed by the included Lānaʻi Air sector when eligible; return positions through HNL before HNL → SFO.
hotels.honestCatch: The island isolation is romantic but creates the highest routing friction in the set, including a mandatory positioning flight before the mainland return.

hotels.honestCatch: It is inland rather than beachfront and more structured wellness retreat than romantic beach resort; choose it only if post-wedding recovery is the trip’s central purpose.

hotels.name: Harbor House Inn
hotels.summary: An eleven-key blufftop inn in remote Elk with five standalone cottages, a private cove, breakfast included, and a two-MICHELIN-star restaurant that gives the stay a true sense of occasion. It is intimate, cinematic, and unusually specific — the best choice if dinner is a central minimoon event.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean View Cottage with private patio for the most privacy and direct water outlook
hotels.priceNote: Generic signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Recent editorial pricing starts around USD 670 before tax; private ocean cottages can cost substantially more. Breakfast is included, but the tasting-menu dinner and wine are separate and material.
hotels.weather: The Mendocino coast in October is cool and changeable: generally low-to-mid 60s by day and around 50°F at night, with wind, fog, and the first meaningful rain systems possible.
hotels.weatherRisk: Medium to high — this is coastal weather rather than Wine Country weather, and outdoor plans may yield to fog, wind, or rain.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then roughly 3 hours 30 minutes to 4 hours via US-101, CA-128, and the last winding Highway 1 segment to Elk. Return the same way to SFO; avoid a tight flight because the coastal road is slow and cell coverage is limited.
hotels.travelFriction: High — no connection required, but the remote, curvy drive is long enough to consume much of arrival and departure day
hotels.honestCatch: Six nights may be too long for such a tiny, remote property unless you want deliberate stillness; restaurant spending can erase the room-rate advantage quickly.

quote.text: Each nightly stay includes a lavish breakfast, access to our private cove, plush down feather bedding, and cozy accommodations.

hotels.name: Meadowood Napa Valley
hotels.summary: A storied 250-acre St. Helena estate with only 36 rooms and suites, exceptional service, three pools, hiking, wellness, and no resort fee. It feels private and established rather than trendy, making it one of the most convincing places to disappear together in Napa.
hotels.bestRoom: Treeline Suite for fireplace, deck, privacy, and a lighter footprint than the very expensive Hill House
hotels.priceNote: October-specific market signal, not a live October 5–11 quote. KAYAK identifies October as the most expensive month, with historical averages around USD 1,831 and weekends around USD 2,220. Meadowood states there is no resort fee; range allows for tax and room choice.
hotels.weather: Harvest-season Napa is usually warm and dry, around 77°F by day and 49°F at night, with only a couple of rainy days across the month.
hotels.weatherRisk: Low to medium — weather is favorable, but heat spikes and wildfire smoke are the real early-fall variables.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then about 2 hours to 2 hours 30 minutes by car through Napa Valley, longer at weekend pinch points. Return to SFO with generous traffic buffer.
hotels.travelFriction: Moderate — simple route, but it is the farthest up-valley Napa option and traffic through the valley is slow
hotels.honestCatch: October harvest pricing presses directly against the hard cap, and the estate’s country-club composure may feel restrained beside the drama of Big Sur or Tofino.

quote.text: A gathering place, private club, and intimate country hotel for generations, our 250-acre wine-country estate invites our guests into the family and community life of Napa Valley.

hotels.name: Solage, Auberge Collection
hotels.summary: A relaxed Calistoga resort built around geothermal bathing, a 20,000-square-foot spa, bicycles, multiple pools, and bright indoor-outdoor rooms. It is the best choice for a true spa agenda and an easygoing rhythm, though it is less private and ceremonious than Meadowood or Farmhouse Inn.
hotels.bestRoom: Orchard Suite for a fireplace, private patio, and outdoor soaking tub
hotels.priceNote: Generic signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Recent public rates range from roughly USD 900 all-in for entry rooms to well above USD 1,500 for premium rooms; October harvest demand and suite choice can push higher.
hotels.weather: Calistoga is warm and dry in early October, often upper 70s by day with crisp nights around 49°F — ideal for pools, bikes, and outdoor dining.
hotels.weatherRisk: Low to medium — heat spikes and North Bay wildfire smoke are more important than rain.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then about 2 hours to 2 hours 30 minutes north by car. The northern Napa location adds valley traffic; allow extra time returning to SFO on Sunday.
hotels.travelFriction: Moderate — straightforward but a long up-valley drive, particularly during harvest weekends
hotels.honestCatch: The 100-room, family-friendly pool scene and casual bungalow plan are fun but not especially secluded; this is a spa vacation first and a hushed honeymoon second.

quote.text: Join us for a Napa Valley escape to detox, retox and repeat.

hotels.name: Stanly Ranch, Auberge Collection
hotels.summary: A large, design-forward ranch at Napa’s southern gateway with contemporary cottages, generous terraces, a serious wellness center, farm-driven food, biking, and easy access to both Napa and Sonoma. It minimizes driving friction but feels social, youthful, and expansive rather than secluded.
hotels.bestRoom: Rambler One-Bedroom King Suite for indoor-outdoor living and enough separation to feel celebratory
hotels.priceNote: Generic signal, not an October 5–11 quote. Current public entry rates begin around USD 950–1,100; a reported USD 86.40 nightly resort fee and local taxes bring the all-in floor higher, while suites and harvest weekends rise sharply.
hotels.weather: Southern Napa in early October is usually sunny and warm, with upper-70s afternoons, cool evenings, and little rain.
hotels.weatherRisk: Low to medium — favorable baseline, with heat and regional smoke the principal exceptions.
hotels.route: MIA → SFO nonstop, then about 1 hour to 1 hour 20 minutes by car via US-101 and CA-37/CA-121. It is the closest Napa contender to SFO and easiest for the outbound flight.
hotels.travelFriction: Low to moderate — the cleanest Wine Country transfer in this set, subject mainly to Bay Area traffic
hotels.honestCatch: At 135 rooms on a 700-plus-acre mixed resort-and-residential development, it can feel like an excellent luxury campus rather than an intimate minimoon secret.

quote.text: Discover a new Napa experience filled with riveting adventures, transformative wellbeing, and farm-driven, elemental cuisine.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Resort Oʻahu at Ko Olina
hotels.summary: A polished west-Oʻahu resort with a calm swimmable lagoon, serious spa and a valuable adults-only infinity pool that creates a genuine couple refuge.
hotels.bestRoom: Prime Oceanfront King, away from connecting-family inventory
hotels.priceNote: No exact-date quote was captured. This broad all-in planning range reflects generic luxury Ko Olina signals and meaningful category spread; confirm taxes, fees and room adjacency.
hotels.weather: Hot, sunny and dry on Oʻahu’s leeward coast, with very good early-October beach weather odds.
hotels.route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Ko Olina is roughly 30–45 minutes from HNL.
hotels.honestCatch: The resort is highly family-oriented and sits beside Disney Aulani; explicitly request a quiet room without a connecting door and away from family-adjacent inventory.

hotels.summary: A composed oceanfront classic with the strongest recent service signal, elegant rooms, La Mer and a calm pool culture despite its urban setting.
hotels.bestRoom: Diamond Head Oceanfront Prime King
hotels.priceNote: No exact Oct 5–11 checkout was captured. This all-in planning range reflects generic public luxury-Waikīkī signals and room-category spread; reprice the Diamond Head category directly.
hotels.weather: Hot and generally sunny in leeward Honolulu, with brief showers possible and lower weather risk than Oʻahu’s North Shore.
hotels.route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Waikīkī is roughly 25–45 minutes from HNL depending on traffic.
hotels.honestCatch: It is an urban Waikīkī grand dame with a small beach footprint, not a secluded resort; city and neighboring-hotel energy remain close.

hotels.name: The Ritz-Carlton Oʻahu, Turtle Bay
hotels.role: The North Shore activity base—bungalow only
hotels.summary: Turtle Bay’s landscape, surfing, horseback riding, golf, hiking and spa are compelling when paired with one of 42 waterfront Ocean Bungalows separated from the 408-room main building.
hotels.bestRoom: Ocean Bungalow King
hotels.priceNote: The resort’s generic October average was around $940, but that does not price the only category recommended here. This all-in bungalow range is directional; eliminate it if the live bungalow total exceeds about $1,800.
hotels.weather: Warm and breezy on Oʻahu’s North Shore, with more passing showers and surf exposure than Ko Olina but less rain risk than Princeville.
hotels.route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Turtle Bay is roughly 60–90 minutes from HNL depending on traffic.
hotels.honestCatch: It is compelling only in an Ocean Bungalow. The main wing is a large family-heavy legacy resort, and recent reviews repeatedly flag slow or uneven service and food.
